newsitem.title: USA: New US crop protection available in major states.
newsitem.headline: New US crop protection available in major states.

text.p: The Agriculture Department announced Friday that three new kinds of crop protection would be available to farmers for 1997 crops.
All use different approaches to protect farmers against low prices and poor yields.
Offered in the largest territory would be Crop Revenue Coverage. It would be available on six crops in major states:
--Corn: Colorado, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, Ohio, Oklahoma, South Dakota and Texas.
--Soybeans: Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, Ohio, Oklahoma, South Dakota and Texas.
--Spring wheat: Minnesota and selected counties in North Dakota and Montana.
--Cotton: Arizona, Georgia, Oklahoma and selected counties in Texas.
--Sorghum: Colorado, Nebraska, Oklahoma and selected counties in Kansas, Missouri and South Dakota.
Income Protection will be offered on five crops in several states.
Territory were Income Protection will be offered was:

--Soybeans: Champaign, Ford, Iroquis, Livingston and MeLean counties in Illinois, Benton, Fountain and Warren counties in Indiana, Adair, Audubo, Cass, Dallas, Guthrie and Shelby counties in Iowa, and selected counties in Arkansas.
--Corn: Champaign, Ford, Iroquis, Livingston and McLean counties in Illinois, Benton, Fountain and Warren counties in Indiana, Adair, Audubon, Cass, Dallas, Guthrie and Shelby counties in Iowa.
--Cotton: Autuaga, Lawrence, Limestone and Madison counties in Alabama and Brooks, Colquitt, Dooly and Worth counties in Georgia.
--Spring wheat: Kittson, Marshall, Polk and Roseau counties in Minnesota and Grand Forks, Pembina and Walsh counties in North Dakota.
Risk assurance, developed by Farm Bureau Mutual Insurance Co, will be available in Iowa for corn and soybean crops.
